title: Composition preserves proper relative diagonals
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every scheme base change is equivalent to an algebraic space. Properties of such maps are tested on these algebraic-space base changes. Let $\mathcal X\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal Y\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal Z$ be morphisms of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$. A morphism $h:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ of these stacks is separated when its relative diagonal $\Delta_h:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal P$ is proper, meaning that for every scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal P$ the 2-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal P}\mathcal P$ is represented by a scheme which is proper over $T$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Equivalently, each such base change, which is an algebraic space locally quasi-finite over $T$, is proper over $T$ in the algebraic-space sense (separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts and universally closed); a proper locally quasi-finite algebraic space over $T$ is finite over $T$, hence a scheme. If both $\Delta_f$ and $\Delta_g$ are proper, then $\Delta_{g\circ f}$ is proper. No properness or finite-type hypothesis on $f$ or $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 050K (lemma-composition-separated), separated case; the diagonal factorization in its proof.

proof.text: Unpack the diagonal on test schemes using the 2-fibre-product definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For a stack morphism $h:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ and a scheme $T$ mapping to $\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal P$, write its datum as $(p_1,p_2,\epsilon:h(p_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}h(p_2))$. On a scheme $T\prime\to T$, the pullback of $\Delta_h$ has objects $(p,a:p\xrightarrow{\sim}p_1,b:p\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2)$ satisfying $h(b)=\epsilon\circ h(a)$. Send this object to $\beta=b\circ a^{-1}$, for which $h(\beta)=\epsilon$. Conversely $\beta$ gives $(p_1,\mathrm{id},\beta)$. An arrow $u:(p,a,b)\to(p',a',b')$ must satisfy $a'\circ u=a$ and $b'\circ u=b$. The first equation forces $u=(a')^{-1}\circ a$; the second holds exactly when $b\circ a^{-1}=b'\circ(a')^{-1}$. Thus an arrow exists exactly when the two values of $\beta$ agree, and then it is unique. Thus these functors give an equivalence with the discrete groupoid of such $\beta$. The formulas commute with restriction to every $T\prime\to T$, hence give an equivalence over $T$. This is an explicit calculation from the definition, not an appeal to a geometric representability theorem.

source.place: Tag 04Z1 (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), the groupoid calculation behind Tag 050H; omitted calculation written out here.

proof.text: Fix any scheme $T$ and map $T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal X$, with datum $(x_1,x_2,\theta:g(f(x_1))\xrightarrow{\sim}g(f(x_2)))$. It induces $T\to\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Y$ with datum $(f(x_1),f(x_2),\theta)$. By the hypothesis on $\Delta_g$, its pullback $E=T\times_{\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y$ is represented by a scheme proper over $T$. By step 1, its points on any $T\prime\to T$ are precisely the isomorphisms $\alpha:f(x_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(x_2)$ with $g(\alpha)=\theta$. This description uses only the 2-fibre-product definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and the stated hypothesis on $\Delta_g$.

source.place: Tag 050K (lemma-composition-separated), factorization of the composite diagonal; Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), its 2-cartesian square, tested over T.

proof.text: Apply the natural description of $E$ in step 2 to its identity $T$-morphism $\mathrm{id}_E:E\to E$. This gives the universal isomorphism $\alpha:f(x_1)|_E\xrightarrow{\sim}f(x_2)|_E$; for every $u:U\to E$, its restriction $u^*\alpha$ is precisely the isomorphism corresponding to $u$. Together with $x_1|_E,x_2|_E$ it defines $E\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$. The hypothesis on $\Delta_f$ therefore makes $V=E\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ a scheme proper over $E$. Step 1 and [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identify its points with $\beta:x_1|_E\xrightarrow{\sim}x_2|_E$ satisfying $f(\beta)=\alpha$. Applying the hypothesis is legitimate because $E$ is a scheme by step 2; no properness assumption on $f$ itself is involved.

source.place: Tag 050K (lemma-composition-separated), the first arrow in the diagonal factorization, after the second arrow has been pulled back to T.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\prime\to T$, the points of $V$ are consequently pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$ satisfying $g(\alpha)=\theta$ and $f(\beta)=\alpha$. Forgetting $\alpha$ is a bijection onto the isomorphisms $\beta:x_1\xrightarrow{\sim}x_2$ with $(g\circ f)(\beta)=\theta$, with inverse $\beta\mapsto(f(\beta),\beta)$. Both formulas commute with every restriction map: restricting a pair sends it to the pair of restrictions, and functoriality of $f$ gives $f(\beta)|_{T\prime}=f(\beta|_{T\prime})$. Between two triples with the same $\beta$, the unique arrow calculated in step 1 is preserved by these formulas. Thus they identify the fibred groupoids, including arrows. By the explicit equivalence of step 1 applied to $h=g\circ f$, this identifies the scheme $V$ over $T$ with the stack $T\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal X}\mathcal X$. The same formulas identify the projection to $T$ with $V\to E\to T$, not merely the underlying sets. This completes the diagonal factorization directly from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 050K (lemma-composition-separated), factorization; Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), with the identification expanded on each test scheme.

proof.text: The maps $V\to E$ and $E\to T$ are proper morphisms of schemes by steps 3 and 2. Their composite $V\to T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Step 4 identifies it with the arbitrary scheme base change of $\Delta_{g\circ f}$. Since $T$ and its map were arbitrary, every such base change is represented by a proper scheme, exactly the separation condition in the statement. This proves the conclusion without a finite-type or properness hypothesis on $f$ or $g$.

source.place: Tag 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper), applied to the two scheme maps produced by the factorization in stacks-morphisms.tex, Tag 050K.

proof.text: Prove also the algebraic-space assertion in the statement. Fix any $h:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ and test datum $(p_1,p_2,\epsilon)$ of step 1. By [lem-sfb-dm-isom-space-unramified], $I_P=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal P}(p_1,p_2)$ and $I_Q=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Q}(h(p_1),h(p_2))$ are algebraic spaces unramified over $T$: both stacks are Deligne--Mumford and both pairs are objects over the same scheme $T$. Applying $h$ to isomorphisms gives a morphism $a:I_P\to I_Q$ over $T$, and $\epsilon$ gives a section $e:T\to I_Q$. Regard $T$ as its represented algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Then $D=I_P\times_{I_Q,e}T$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its points are exactly $\beta$ with $h(\beta)=\epsilon$, naturally on every $T$-scheme, so the equivalence of step 1 identifies $D$ over $T$ with the scheme base change of $\Delta_h$.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal); stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06N3 (theorem-DM) and 06MB (lemma-properties-covering-imply-diagonal); spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces).

proof.text: The composite $I_P\xrightarrow{a}I_Q\to T$ is the unramified structure map from step 6. The cancellation clause of [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence] therefore makes $a$ unramified, with no hypothesis on $h$ or on $I_Q\to T$ needed for cancellation. The base-change clause makes $D\to T$ unramified. For every representable etale scheme chart $V\to D$, the same node gives that $V\to D$ is unramified and that its composite $V\to T$ is unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to this morphism of schemes: it is locally quasi-finite at every point. Thus $D\to T$ is locally quasi-finite in precisely the every-etale-scheme-chart sense required below. No quasi-compactness, finite presentation or finite-type hypothesis on $h$ was used.

For the remaining equivalence, more generally let $A\to T$ be any chartwise locally quasi-finite algebraic space over a scheme. Suppose it is proper in the algebraic-space sense stated in the item. In particular its diagonal is a closed immersion after every scheme base change, so [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] gives a scheme $Z$ representing $A$ over $T$. For represented maps the scheme and space properness tests agree: use the identity scheme charts of [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; separatedness is the same diagonal condition, finite type is the same quasi-compact/local-finite-type condition, and universal closedness is the same closedness condition after every scheme base change [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Consequently $Z\to T$ is proper. Conversely a proper scheme representative satisfies those very same tests and makes $A\to T$ proper. Taking the identity chart $Z\to A$ in the assumed chartwise local quasi-finiteness gives that $Z\to T$ is locally quasi-finite. Hence [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes $Z\to T$ finite. Thus every proper locally quasi-finite algebraic space over $T$ is finite and a scheme. Apply this to the $D$ of steps 6--7: being proper as an algebraic space is equivalent to having a proper scheme representative, which proves every clause of the retained Equivalently sentence.
